title: 5.2.7 Worked Example: Falling Block
description: A dynamic block falls under gravity and lands on the static ground. Read the example, then experiment. Follows 5.2.6 (Reading: Gravity).

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: Click Run. The block falls and the ground catches it.
hints: Static sprites don't move; they push back on dynamic ones.

steps.title: Turn gravity off, then up
steps.instructions: Change `world.gravity.y = 10` to `world.gravity.y = 0` and Run. The block floats. Then change it to `world.gravity.y = 20` and Run again. The block falls faster. Leave it at 20 for the next steps.
hints: Gravity units are roughly pixels per second².

steps.title: Make the ground dynamic
steps.instructions: With gravity still on, remove the `'static'` argument from the ground sprite. Both pieces fall now: that's why the ground is static.
hints: new Sprite(x, y, w, h) defaults to dynamic. Add 'static' to anchor it.

steps.title: Add a second falling block
steps.instructions: Declare another sprite and color it differently. Watch them stack.
hints: Give them different x positions so they don't spawn on top of each other.

requirements.title: You changed the gravity
requirements.description: End with `world.gravity.y` set to a number other than 10 (step 2 uses 20). Help: 5.2.6 (Reading: Gravity)
